content:
“Secure sea lanes, freedom of navigation, respect for international law and unhindered maritime trade are pivotal for collective security & prosperity of the Indian Ocean Region (IOR),” stated Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh as he called for enhanced cooperation between India and Sri Lanka to shape a favourable and secure maritime environment and tackle emerging maritime challenges before they evolve into serious threats to developmental interests and brighter future. He was addressing a gathering comprising Sri Lankan Deputy Minister of Defence Mr Aruna Jayasekara, Commanders of the Sri Lankan Army, Navy & Air Force, and other senior officials during his visit to the country’s Ministry of Defence in Colombo on September 09, 2026.
Raksha Mantri asserted that national security and economic growth cannot be viewed in isolation as they are intrinsically linked to geography and security, emphasising that neither country can afford to remain indifferent to the developments in the region. He stated that while India and Sri Lanka have upgraded their capabilities through a series of measures ranging from capacity building to joint exercises, there is a need to further strengthen the longstanding  India-Sri Lanka defence and strategic partnership with special emphasis on maritime cooperation.
“We need to devise & implement joint protocols, sharpen the skills and share experiences to deal with emerging threats arising from the rapidly evolving global and regional dynamics. It needs to be a continuous process. We must develop new paradigms for a closer and stronger maritime partnership, which is the basis of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s vision of MAHASAGAR (Mutual and Holistic Advancement for Security and Growth Across Regions). ‘Mutual’ and ‘Holistic’ underscore the importance of synergy, cooperation and collaboration,” stated Shri Rajnath Singh.
Raksha Mantri stated that India and Sri Lanka are bound by the shared ocean, and maritime security is not a matter of abstract theory but a reality that shapes their trade, security and destinies. “Sri Lanka is a friendly neighbour, longstanding friend and reliable partner for India. Both nations are central to any strategic discourse on maritime security in the region. Strong India-Sri Lanka maritime cooperation will be mutually beneficial and vital for collective growth and security,” he said.
Shri Rajnath Singh highlighted the significant progress achieved in bilateral maritime cooperation, particularly in Search & Rescue Operations that have saved numerous precious lives at sea. He added that both nations have been working together in the fields of counter-narcotics, anti-piracy and human trafficking. “In this regard, our mutual association in Colombo Security Conclave which focuses on maritime safety, counter-terrorism, cyber security and organised crime becomes more relevant than ever before,” he said.
Raksha Mantri described the commissioning of the Maritime Rescue Coordination Centre, established through the collaboration between the two countries, as an excellent example of their shared commitment towards keeping the waters of the Indian Ocean safe and secure. “India stands ready to join hands with Sri Lanka in areas such as capacity building and joint exercises, enabling both sides to learn from each other’s experiences and fine-tune protocols for the effective implementation of joint initiatives. We’re committed to assisting Sri Lanka in every possible way to further strengthen such cooperation,” he said.
Shri Rajnath Singh envisaged a future where India and Sri Lanka emerge as joint stakeholders in developing a mutually beneficial and integrated Maritime Domain Awareness system, providing comprehensive maritime information on a real-time basis. “This would entail systematic cooperation and interaction amongst concerned agencies, navies and coast guards of the two countries with a view to addressing the challenges of illegal fishing, suspicious vessels tracking, narcotics trafficking, smuggling, terrorism and other security threats,” he said.
Referring to the challenges faced by our fishermen, Raksha Mantri underscored that the issue needs to be addressed together. He observed that maritime cooperation should extend beyond the security framework to also cover areas like aquaculture, marine biotechnology, ocean science, protection and preservation of maritime environment and maritime tourism. He also suggested that the two countries can explore the establishment of a joint Maritime Humanitarian Assistance & Disaster Relief (HADR) system involving relevant agencies for a coordinated and rapid response to natural calamities and man-made disasters.
Shri Rajnath Singh asserted that as the Indian Ocean enters a period of profound strategic and economic transformation, India and Sri Lanka must synergise their efforts, build upon their collective competencies and address emerging challenges together. “The tectonic shifts and rapid transformation underway present both challenges and opportunities. The two countries must leverage their longstanding maritime partnership to turn these opportunities into shared growth,” he said.
Raksha Mantri noted that the future of India-Sri Lanka relations should be anchored in the simple premise that proximity creates interdependence, which in turn creates immense opportunities for shared evolution. Describing India as a true Vishwa Mitra, or trusted global friend, he reiterated India’s commitment to playing a constructive and dependable role in its shared neighbourhood. Holistic maritime security and mutual prosperity are two sides of the same coin, he said. He expressed confidence that India and Sri Lanka, as close maritime partners, are well positioned to jointly safeguard peace, security and stability across the IOR.
High Commissioner of India to Sri Lanka Shri Santosh Jha and other senior officials were present on the occasion.
Upon his arrival at the Ministry of Defence, Shri Rajnath Singh was accorded a Guard of Honour. He also laid a wreath at the Indian Peace Keeping Force (IPKF) Memorial in Battaramulla and paid homage to the bravehearts who made the supreme sacrifice in the line of duty.

The program is a collaborative effort involving CMLRE (MoES), the International Seabed Authority (ISA), the Indian Ocean Rim Association (IORA), and the National Marine Biodiversity Institute of Korea (MABIK).
Inaugural Highlights and Leadership Addresses
The inaugural ceremony was graced by Her Excellency
Ms. Leticia Carvalho
, Secretary-General of the International Seabed Authority (ISA), as the Chief Guest. Delivering an inspirational address, Ms. Carvalho emphasized the critical need to strengthen scientific knowledge and taxonomic expertise to underpin sound environmental management of the deep seabed. She underscored the role of international cooperation and standardized scientific approaches among member states, while encouraging early-career researchers to cultivate scientific excellence, perseverance, and confidence when embracing complex challenges.
Earlier, the welcome address was delivered by
Dr. R. Maheskumar
, Head of CMLRE. The inaugural session featured a comprehensive presentation on the multi-spectrum marine biodiversity research activities of CMLRE by
Dr. Senthil
, Scientist-E, CMLRE, followed by a Special Lecture on marine biodiversity studies under MoES's Deep Ocean Mission by
Dr. G. Dharani
, Scientist-G & Head of the Marine Biotechnology Division at NIOT, Chennai. The ceremony also spotlighted institutional activities and commitments under the SSKI program by MABIK, Republic of Korea, alongside a keynote address by
Dr. Baban Ingole
, former Scientist at NIO, Goa, focusing on benthic studies in the Indian Ocean.
Global Participation and Technical Scope
The training program brings together approximately 30 early-career researchers and scientists from ISA Member States within the Indian Ocean Region (IORA). Participating nations include South Africa, Kenya, Bangladesh, Mauritius, Malaysia, Indonesia, Singapore, Sri Lanka, Mozambique, Tanzania, Thailand, Oman, and India.
Over the five-day intensive curriculum, participants will engage in:
Specialized lectures, field visits, and benthic sample collection
Hands-on laboratory training in macrofauna identification and result reporting
Advanced technical instruction in traditional taxonomy, DNA barcoding, Scanning Electron Microscopy (SEM), and biodiversity data analysis
Workshops on sample curation and open-access biodiversity data publishing
Guidance is being provided by eminent national and international resource persons hailing from Brazil, South Korea, Portugal, Sweden, Mauritius, Indonesia, Germany, and Singapore, alongside experts from collaborating Indian institutions and CMLRE.
Strategic Importance
Hosting this landmark ISA capacity-building program reinforces India’s growing leadership in deep-sea biodiversity research. By standardizing methodologies for benthic biodiversity assessment and fostering robust international scientific partnerships, the initiative marks a significant step forward in sustainable Indian Ocean exploration and environmental governance.

content:
Kolkata, September 09, 2026 — Marking a historic milestone in India’s journey toward self-reliance in oceanographic science and maritime technology, the state-of-the-art Ocean Research Vessel (Yard 3041), officially named ORV Sagar Manthan, was launched today at the Rishi Bankim Shipyard, Kolkata.
Designed, engineered, and constructed by defense public sector undertaking Garden Reach Shipbuilders & Engineers Limited (GRSE) for the National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR), under the Ministry of Earth Sciences (MoES), the vessel was officially launched through virtual presence by Dr. Jitendra Singh, Hon’ble Minister of Earth Sciences, Government of India, with his spouse Mrs Manju Singh, who named the vessel, keeping with the tradition. The event was held in the august presence of Dr T. Srinivasa Kumar, Secretary, Ministry of Earth Sciences, Government of India, who was joined by his spouse,
Mrs Kavita Ellanti, for the ship launch in Kolkata.
Hon'ble Minister highlighted National Pride, Global Ocean Geopolitics, and Atmanirbharta. Delivering the keynote address (virtual), Dr Jitendra Singh, Hon’ble Minister of Earth Sciences, termed the occasion a "red letter day" for NCPOR, the Ministry, and the nation. He praised the team for achieving the launch within just two years of contract signing and barely five months after keel laying, hailing it as an exceptional display of efficiency.
Highlighting the strategic and scientific necessity of the vessel, Dr Jitendra Singh (through his message) conveyed: "
This fine ship is India’s first advanced Ocean Research Vessel built by GRSE, displaying the required thrust towards Atmanirbharta and self-reliance that Hon'ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi Ji has been laying so much stress on. Knowledge is strength, and this knowledge can only be gained through research. Today, the world knows very little about our oceans, yet they provide vital inputs about melting polar glaciers, maritime impact, and climate dynamics. Solid data collected by vessels like ORV Sagar Manthan will allow India to lead the global path in disaster prevention, take corrective environmental measures, and play a pivotal role in global ocean geopolitics.
"
Dr Singh noted that the feature-rich ORV Sagar Manthan will gradually replace the iconic 43-year-old ORV Sagar Kanya (procured from Germany in 1983), commending MoES plans to acquire more oceanographic vessels and a Polar Research Vessel in the near future.
MoES Secretary emphasised Scientific Capabilities and Indigenous Transition
In his address, Dr T. Srinivasa Kumar, Secretary, Ministry of Earth Sciences, expressed pride in India’s policy shift from acquiring research platforms abroad to building them domestically.
Elaborating the core scientific impact, Dr T. Srinivasa Kumar remarked:
"
As an oceanographer, I have witnessed first-hand the immense value of ocean research. It is the foundation for understanding climate challenges, predicting tsunamis, and strengthening maritime capabilities. The capabilities of this new ORV excite me as a scientist. It will feature underway swath multibeam surveys, geophysical profiling, atmospheric observations, and water column sampling. GRSE has passed a complex challenge with flying colours, proving that India is among the select few nations capable of designing and constructing such complex platforms.
"
Project Background and Strategic Significance
Constructed under Vertical-4 (Deep Ocean Survey and Exploration) of the Government of India's flagship Deep Ocean Mission (DOM) at an approximate cost of Rs. 840 Crore, ORV Sagar Manthan is an all-weather, multidisciplinary platform. It is engineered to operate in extreme oceanic environments, including the Southern Ocean, with a projected service life of 30 years.
Key Technical & Operational Features
Advanced Equipment: Integrated with dynamic positioning, multibeam bathymetry, multichannel seismic systems, sub-bottom profiling, weather radar, drop keels, and deployment facilities for Remotely Operated Vehicles (ROV) and Autonomous Underwater Vehicles (AUV).
Research Spectrum: Will support multidisciplinary exploration along the Indian Ocean mid-oceanic ridges to identify multi-metal hydrothermal sulphide mineralisation, establish environmental baselines, collect upper-air data, and undertake CTD profiling.
Dual-Class Certification: Built in full compliance with international regulatory standards under dual-class certification by the Indian Register of Shipping (IRS) and the American Bureau of Shipping (ABS).
Project Milestones: Following contract signing in July 2024, first steel cutting on November 29, 2024, and Keel Laying on April 08, 2026, the vessel successfully transitioned from the erection dock to the construction dock today.
Following its launch, superstructure erection, system integration, and extensive sea trials will proceed before its final delivery for commissioning to NCPOR/MoES, which is scheduled for 2028.
The ceremony featured key ceremonial milestones conducted by distinguished dignitaries. After the welcome address by Cmdr PR Hari, C&MD, GRSE, the Launching & Naming Ceremony of Yard 3041 through the official Unveiling of the Name Plaque was done in the presence of Dr MV Ramanamurthy, Mission Director, Deep Ocean Mission and Dr Thamban Meloth, Director, NCPOR, MoES.  Marking the flagship moment of the occasion, the formal Launching of the Ship was successfully executed by officially transferring the advanced vessel into the water to begin its next phase of construction.

title: UIDAI Launches Aadhaar Face Authentication SDK and Sandbox at Global Fintech Fest 2026
subtitle:
Makes it easier for BFSI sector players to use Aadhaar face authentication for RBI-mandated multi-factor authentication

Users journey simplified: reduces the need for multiple apps for Aadhaar Face Authentication
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                09 SEP 2026 6:15PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Unique Identification Authority of India (UIDAI) on Wednesday launched the Aadhaar Face Authentication SDK (Software Development Kit) and Aadhaar Face Authentication Sandbox at the Global Fintech Fest 2026, enabling ecosystem partners to integrate, test and deploy Aadhaar Face Authentication more seamlessly within their digital applications.
The Aadhaar Face Authentication SDK brings UIDAI’s Face Authentication capability directly into native Android and iOS applications. It eliminates the need for users to switch between applications, enabling a smoother, single-app authentication experience.
The ready-to-use SDK simplifies integration for ecosystem partners while incorporating AI/ML-based liveness and anti-spoofing capabilities. It also supports secure handling and encryption of authentication data and is designed to work across consumer smartphones. The SDK is expected to help government departments, banks, fintechs and other organisations deploy Face Authentication-enabled services more efficiently.
Alongside the SDK, UIDAI also launched the Aadhaar Face Authentication Sandbox, a secure and controlled environment that allows organisations to integrate, test and validate the complete Face Authentication journey before production onboarding.
The Sandbox enables developers and quality assurance teams to test key stages, including user provisioning and consent, face capture, liveness checks, authentication, error handling, and response validation-- without requiring external biometric hardware. It also allows testing of failure scenarios such as invalid digital signatures, network interruptions, timeouts and spoofing attempts.
The launch of the SDK and Sandbox fulfills a long-standing demand of the Fintech and banking ecosystem to build a seamless, and secure user onboarding journey from within the user bank/fintech organisation’s mobile application.
It simplifies the journey. The user downloads only one app, say a banking/ insurance/  broking app and does Aadhaar authentication from within the app. Earlier, for a similar experience, a background app called FaceRD app was needed. This made the user onboarding journey longer and dependent on the presence of the Aadhaar FaceRD app.  With this launch, it reduces the need for multiple apps for Aadhaar Face Authentication
UIDAI’s indigenously engineered AI/ML-driven Face Authentication solution, which was launched in 2021, has processed over 500 crore transactions and been adopted by nearly 200 entities, including Union Government ministries and departments, State Governments, Banks, NBFCs, telecom operators, brokerage firms and certifying authorities among others. The technology received the Prime Minister’s Award for Excellence in Public Administration 2023 under the Innovation category.
Face Authentication is widely used across services like submission of Digital Life Certificate (Jeevan Pramaan) by pensioners, Ayushman Bharat beneficiary onboarding, DBT schemes, Aadhaar-enabled payments, SIM activation through e-KYC, beneficiary authentication for schemes like PM e-Drive, PM Awas Yojana and PM Kisan etc.
UIDAI also unveiled a “Playbook on ease of Onboarding” which will work as a guide for BFSI entities to get onboarded in the UIDAI authentication ecosystem for ID verification of its customers, staff, and other business partners.

title: CAQM takes serious note of HSPCB’s non-compliance with its directions; Seeks explanation in review meeting
ministry: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                09 SEP 2026 12:39PM by PIB Delhi
content:
A review meeting was held on 08.09.2026 under the Chairmanship of Shri Rajesh Verma, Chairperson, Commission for Air Quality Management in NCR and Adjoining Areas (CAQM), with the Haryana State Pollution Control Board (HSPCB) regarding compliance with the Commission’s Statutory Directions, which mandate the registration of all C&D projects having a plot area of 500 sq. metres or above and the installation of functional video monitoring systems on the State/GNCTD web portal for remote monitoring of dust mitigation measures.
CAQM has been undertaking sample-based remote monitoring of C&D sites through the web portal of the HSPCB since 2024. During the monitoring exercises, several discrepancies have been observed, including incomplete/ insufficient web-camera links, incorrect User ID/ Password, links prompting installation of mobile applications, non-working web links and cameras remaining offline despite successful login. These discrepancies have been communicated to HSPCB from time to time for necessary corrective action(s).
During the remote monitoring exercise conducted by CAQM through the HSPCB portal from 19.06.2026 to 22.06.2026, it was observed that out of 213 active C&D sites registered in Panipat, 457 in Sonipat, 168 in Faridabad, 691 in Gurugram (North) and 484 in Gurugram (South), web-camera links at most of the sites were found to be non-functional. Functional links were available only at 4 sites in Faridabad, 6 sites in Gurugram (North) and 5 sites in Gurugram (South). The observations were communicated to HSPCB on 08.07.2026.
CAQM has also earlier advised HSPCB to deploy a dedicated team for effective remote monitoring through the portal. However, neither such team was deployed nor any substantial improvement was observed. The non-functioning of web-camera links has consequently defeated the very purpose of the web portal for effective remote monitoring of C&D sites and verification of dust-control measures.
Taking serious note of the continued discrepancies and non-compliance by HSPCB, the Commission has treated the matter as willful non-compliance on the part of the designated authority responsible for enforcement of the Commission’s Directions. CAQM called upon HSPCB for the review meeting, to furnish the requisite information, detailed response and report with respect to the notices issued to it, indicating the complete status of compliance. In response, HSPCB apprised the Commission of the compliance status and the steps undertaken towards implementation of CAQM’s Statutory Directions.
Further, in the review meeting, HSPCB has been directed to ensure strict compliance with all Order(s)/ Statutory Direction(s) issued by the Commission and to take necessary corrective measures including closure of non-compliant sites, for ensuring effective and uninterrupted remote monitoring of C&D sites. The concerned authorities were also directed to strengthen monitoring and enforcement mechanisms so that the prescribed dust mitigation measures are effectively implemented at C&D sites.
The Commission reiterated that effective implementation of its Statutory Directions by concerned agencies is critical for prevention and abatement of air pollution in NCR. CAQM emphasised that concerned agencies must ensure timely compliance with the Order(s)/ Statutory Direction(s) issued by CAQM in letter and spirit and strengthen monitoring & enforcement mechanism for effective on-ground implementation. The Commission will continue to closely monitor compliance and take necessary measures towards effective mitigation of air pollution in the region.

title: DRI seizes two leopard pelts; 180 live Indian star tortoises; 12 live tokay geckos; around 24 kg pangolin scales and 500 grams tiger bones

date:

content:
Continuing its intelligence-led crackdown on the illegal trafficking of protected wildlife and wildlife derivatives, the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI) conducted six significant operations at different locations across the country in last 10 days, resulting in the seizure of a two leopard pelts, 180 live Indian Star Tortoises, 12 live Tokay Geckos, around 24 kg Pangolin Scales and 500 grams Tiger bones. Thirteen persons were arrested across these six operations.
In an intelligence led operation on 07.09.2026, officers of DRI, in Jeypore, Koraput district, Odisha, intercepted a person and recovered
one leopard pelt
from his possession. Leopards are protected under Schedule I of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972, and trade, sale, purchase, possession or transportation of their pelts or parts is prohibited. The leopard pelt and the apprehended person were handed over to the State Forest Department, Koraput, for further investigation and legal action under the Act.
In another operation on the same day, officers of DRI intercepted a person   near Gandhinagar, Bengaluru and examination of his baggage resulted in the recovery of
180 live Indian Star Tortoises
concealed in six cloth covers. The species was identified by the Wildlife Crime Control Bureau (WCCB) as
Geochelone Elegan
and is listed under Schedule I of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972. The striking star-like pattern on the shell of the Indian Star Tortoise has made it particularly attractive in the exotic pet and wildlife-collector markets, driving illegal capture and international trafficking. The 180 live tortoises were seized under the Act and the accused was arrested.
In the third operation on 07.09.2026, officers of DRI, intercepted a Bolero truck   in Ri-Bhoi district, Meghalaya, while it was proceeding towards Mawhati. Thorough checking of the vehicle led to the recovery of
14.68 kg dried Pangolin
scales, packed in three carry bags. Pangolins are protected under Schedule I of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972 and are also listed in Appendix I of CITES. Pangolins are among the most heavily trafficked mammals in the world, with their scales primarily sought for use in traditional medicine in parts of Asia. The recovered pangolin scales, along with the apprehended person and the vehicle, were handed over to the Range Forest Officer, Nongpoh, Meghalaya, for further necessary action.
Earlier, on 05–06.09.2026, DRI officers, in in an operation targeting an illegal leopard skin trade network, coordinated with the Forest Department, Sidhi, Madhya Pradesh and intercepted four persons in Sidhi district.
One leopard skin
was recovered from two persons travelling in a Mahindra Thar.  Follow-up investigations and searches led to the identification and interception of two further members of the syndicate, besides recovery of incriminating evidence relating to the alleged illegal poaching, possession, transportation and proposed sale of leopard skin and its parts. The leopard skin and vehicle were seized and the persons were handed over to the Forest Department, Sidhi, for further action under the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972.
On 05.09.2026, DRI officers, acting on specific intelligence regarding an illegal wildlife trade, intercepted two persons, in Keokhali, Assam and recovered
12 live Tokay Geckos
from their possession. The Tokay Gecko is listed under Schedule I of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972 and CITES Appendix II. Tokay Geckos are trafficked mainly for their use in traditional medicine in parts of Asia, particularly in dried form,   but also has some demand as an exotic pet. The live geckos were seized under the Act and the two apprehended persons, along with the wildlife articles, were handed over to the Range Forest Officer, Biswanath Wildlife Division, Assam, for further action.
Earlier, on 28.08.2026, DRI officers in Karbi Anglong district, intercepted three persons travelling in a vehicle, and the operation resulted in the recovery of  around 9 kg Pangolin scales and approximately 0.5 kg of Tiger bone set with skull and teeth. The recovered wildlife articles and vehicle were seized under the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972, and the three persons were handed over to the Forest Range Officer, Bokolia, Assam, for further necessary action.
The diverse recoveries — from live endangered wildlife to animal skins, pangolin scales and tiger parts — also demonstrate the varied forms in which wildlife is trafficked and the need for sustained inter-agency coordination.
DRI has been successfully disrupting wildlife trafficking networks and protecting India's rich biodiversity through coordinated, intelligence-driven enforcement under the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972, in close cooperation with the Forest Departments, WCCB, and other enforcement agencies.

The farmer who has always fed this nation is now also lighting it up with the Annadata becoming an Urjadata, said Union Minister for New and Renewable Energy, Education and Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution, Shri Pralhad Joshi, while addressing the curtain-raiser event ahead of the 7th Agrivoltaics World Conference 2026 in New Delhi today.
The Union Minister said the next phase of PM-KUSUM will carry a dedicated component for agrivoltaics, enabling farmers to continue farming while also earning from electricity. He said the focus will be on small and marginal farmers, Farmer Producer Organisations, cooperatives and panchayats, while ensuring that land ownership remains with the farmer. He said solar income can provide greater income security to farmers whose earnings are otherwise dependent on monsoons and market prices.
Shri Joshi said that a farmer can earn three streams of income from the same acre — from the crop sold, the power sold to the DISCOM, and the money saved on diesel. For a small farmer, solar income is not just extra income, it is security, he said, adding that it can provide a regular source of income in both good years and bad years.
The Minister noted that India has about 18% of the world’s population but a 2.4% of world’s land, with more than 85% of farmers being small and marginal farmers cultivating less than 2 hectares. With agrivoltaics, he said, we do not have to choose between crop and solar plant, we can do both at the same time.
The same land can continue to grow crops below, while generating clean energy above.
The Minister said India added 55.29 GW of non-fossil capacity last year, more than the entire installed power capacity of several developed countries: Norway (40.6 GW), Switzerland (around 30 GW), Austria (34 GW) and Belgium (around 33 GW).
Shri Joshi highlighted the progress under PM-KUSUM, stating that around 29 lakh pumps have been solarised. He added that last year, decentralised solar contributed 16.3 GW, comprising 7.6 GW from PM-KUSUM and 8.7 GW of rooftop solar, largely under PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana, which is touching 5.6 million beneficiaries.
The Union Minister highlighted the need for more research on Agrivoltaics to understand what works best for different crops, climates and regions. He gave the example of BAIF's Rural Innovation Centre in Pune where researchers are testing 17 solar configurations across 30 crops, underscoring the importance of finding the right combination of crop, panel height, spacing, tracking system and business model for each farming condition.
Shri Joshi urged stakeholders, including industry and innovators, to focus on structures that allow tractors and harvesters to move freely and withstand local weather conditions, crop-wise and region-wise data generation by ICAR, agricultural universities and Krishi Vigyan Kendras, and innovation in structures, materials and mounting systems to narrow the cost gap with conventional solar. He said India is already building village-level skills and has trained almost 70,000 Surya Mitras.
The Minister said India’s experience in agrivoltaics can be particularly relevant to the Global South, where farms have small holdings, abundant sunshine and grids that are still catching up. He said India’s scale provides an opportunity to develop affordable and practical solutions that can be replicated across the Global South.
During the Curtain Raiser, the Union Minister also launched the teaser of the 7th Agrivoltaics World Conference 2026 along with the unveiling of the official Conference logo. The Agrivoltaics Pitch Hub on the theme “Fueling Farm to Fork Innovations” was also announced with the National Solar Energy Federation of India (NSEFI) as the knowledge partner. Built around the 3F framework of Food, Fuel and Fibre, the Pitch Hub will invite innovative solutions that can contribute to the future of agrivoltaics.
Several national and international stakeholders, along with senior officials and representatives from Ministries, State Departments, research and industry sectors, were present during the Curtain Raiser.
The 7th Agrivoltaics World Conference 2026 will be held from 21st to 23rd October 2026 at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi. The three-day international conference will bring together farmers, policymakers, researchers, industry leaders, international delegations and other stakeholders from across the world to deliberate on the future of agrivoltaics and explore pathways for scaling the sector.
The Conference is expected to provide an important platform for global and national stakeholders to exchange experiences, foster partnerships and identify practical pathways for integrating agriculture and solar energy. It will seek to advance farmer-centric, sustainable and scalable agrivoltaics solutions while strengthening India’s role in shaping the global discourse on the sector.

content:
Himachal Pradesh Chief Minister Shri Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu called on Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science & Technology and Earth Sciences, and MoS PMO, Personnel, Public Grievances, Pensions, Atomic Energy and Space, Dr. Jitendra Singh, in New Delhi today and discussed a range of issues concerning the State, including strengthening weather observation and early-warning systems, expansion of lavender cultivation under the CSIR Aroma Mission, grassroots-level weather forecasting, the possibility of a high-altitude sky observatory in Spiti, and issues related to the Himachal Pradesh State cadre.
During the meeting, the Chief Minister appreciated and thanked the Government led by Prime Minister Narendra Modi for five Doppler Weather Radars support for Himachal Pradesh, while discussing the need to further strengthen the State's weather observation and early-warning capabilities. Dr. Jitendra Singh stressed that necessary steps should be taken to ensure that Himachal Pradesh has an adequate early-warning system, particularly keeping in view its difficult mountainous terrain and vulnerability to extreme weather events. The meeting also covered the proposed expansion of the weather observation network in the State.
Chief Secretary of Himachal Pradesh Shri Kamlesh Kumar Pant and senior officials were also present during the meeting.
Himachal Pradesh currently has three Doppler Weather Radars, at Kufri, Jot and Murari Devi, while two more are in the pipeline, making the total five. The proposed expansion includes two additional Doppler Weather Radars, one in Lahaul-Spiti and another in Kinnaur.
The existing IMD observational network in the State also includes 28 Automatic Weather Stations, 64 Automatic Rain Gauges and 84 Daily Rainfall Monitoring Stations.
The proposed expansion also includes 20 Automatic Weather Stations, 24 Automatic Rain Gauges, 21 Automatic Snow Gauges and one Radio Sonde/Radio Wind system. Suitable sites for the proposed radars in Lahaul-Spiti and Kinnaur are currently being examined, with site selection facing technical issues related to beam blockage.
The discussions also covered the Gram Panchayat-level weather forecast being provided by the India Meteorological Department, aimed at taking location-specific weather information closer to people at the grassroots. The service, known as Mausamgram, provides weather forecasts at Gram Panchayat level and is designed to make localised weather information available for everyday decision-making, including for farmers.
Dr. Jitendra Singh also discussed the expansion of the successful lavender cultivation model under the CSIR Aroma Mission in Himachal Pradesh. Under Phase III of the CSIR Aroma Mission, CSIR-IIIM Jammu has extended lavender cultivation to Upper Bhamla, Tehsil Baldwara, District Mandi, where 20,000 lavender cuttings have been planted and around 150 farmers have been associated with the initiative. The initial trials have been successful, and more area is proposed to be brought under lavender cultivation this season. Distillation units are also proposed to be provided to farmers under Phase IV of the Aroma Mission.
The Minister also referred to the expansion of the lavender initiative beyond Jammu & Kashmir, including Nagaland, Uttarakhand and Arunachal Pradesh, with the model seeking to connect cultivation with industry and value addition so that farmers can derive greater livelihood benefits from the crop.
Another key issue discussed was the possibility of establishing a high-altitude sky observatory in Spiti. The proposal is being explored in consultation with the Indian Institute of Astrophysics, taking advantage of the region's high-altitude location and favourable conditions for astronomical observations. The proposed concept envisages a scientific facility that can also support students and educational activities, while opening up opportunities for astro-tourism and stargazing.
The discussions included the possibility of combining a telescope facility for scientific studies and use by college students with smaller telescope-based facilities that could enable tourists to experience stargazing. A detailed proposal from the Indian Institute of Astrophysics is expected to take the initiative forward.
The meeting also covered issues related to the Himachal Pradesh State cadre, including matters arising from the cadre review process. The discussions were confined to the issues concerning the State and the appropriate procedural course of action, without indicating any final decision on cadre strength or restructuring.
The discussions reflected the potential of science and technology interventions to address some of Himachal Pradesh's distinctive challenges—from timely weather warnings in its vulnerable mountain regions and technology-led livelihood opportunities for farmers, to scientific exploration and new tourism opportunities in high-altitude areas.

title: NHAI Tightens Compliance Norms for Plantation Before Issuance of Provisional Certificate of Completion for National Highway Projects
subtitle: New guidelines mandate minimum 80% plantation coverage and 90% survival rate along National Highways
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                09 SEP 2026 4:47PM by PIB Delhi
content:
To ensure strict compliance with contractual obligations related to plantation along the median and avenues of National Highway projects, National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) has issued comprehensive guidelines mandating plantation and landscaping as integral components of National Highway development and overall project completion.
Under the new guidelines, NHAI will ensure that median and avenue plantation is undertaken strictly in accordance with the respective contract/concession agreement and prescribed guidelines as per the Green Highways Policy, 2015; IRC:SP:21-2009 and other relevant guidelines issued by Ministry of Road Transport and Highways and NHAI.
A key provision of the guidelines is the introduction of a minimum threshold for issuance of the Provisional Certificate of Completion (PCC) / Provisional Commercial Operation Date (PCOD). Plantation works will be considered compliant for the purpose of provisional completion certification only when plantation has been undertaken on least 80% of the available Right of Way (ROW) earmarked for plantation, with planted saplings recording a minimum survival rate of 90% at the time of inspection by the officials.
The guidelines further stipulate that any plantation shortfall beyond the prescribed 80% threshold must be highlighted along with specific timelines for completion. Appropriate financial withholdings, as provided under the relevant Contract/Concession Agreement, will be enforced until the balance plantation is completed and the prescribed target is fully achieved.
NHAI has also strengthened plantation maintenance requirements during the Operations and Maintenance (O&M) period of the National Highways. The release of O&M/annuity payments in Engineering, Procurement and Construction (EPC), Hybrid Annuity Mode (HAM) and Build-Operate-Transfer (BOT) Annuity projects, as well as assessment of maintenance compliance in BOT-Toll projects will be subject to maintaining a minimum 90% survival rate throughout the O&M period.
The guidelines also mandate timely plant casualty replacement to ensure sustained plantation density. In cases of plant mortality, replacement shall be undertaken with plants of similar age and growth, thereby maintaining uniformity and continuity of the plantation along the National Highway corridor. Before processing O&M/annuity payments or certifying maintenance compliance, NHAI will seek technical assistance from environment & plantation expert, engaged by NHAI to verify field-level compliance and ensure adherence to the prescribed plant survival standards.
NHAI had earlier observed that development of plantation along the Median and Avenues, which is a contractual obligation, was often not accorded due importance at the time of issuing PCC/PCOD for National Highway projects. The rerevised guidelines reinforce NHAI’s commitment to integrate environmental sustainability and plantation management into core implementation and maintenance framework of National Highway projects.

title: Self-assembly of organic molecules opens a new path to green hydrogen production
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                09 SEP 2026 5:02PM by PIB Delhi
content:
A simple yet powerful strategy of integrating naturally occurring amino acid with a light-absorbing organic molecule could improve solar driven hydrogen production using completely metal free organic materials.
Hydrogen is considered one of the most promising clean energy carriers because its combustion produces only water, making it an environmentally benign alternative to fossil fuels. One of the promising methods for producing green hydrogen is by using sunlight to split water into hydrogen and oxygen. However, most existing photocatalysts rely on inorganic semiconductors or precious metals, which are often expensive, difficult to manufacture, and raise concerns regarding long-term sustainability. Developing efficient metal-free organic photocatalysts has therefore remained a major scientific challenge.
A team of researchers from the Centre for Nano and Soft Matter Sciences (CeNS), Bengaluru, -an autonomous institute under Department of Science and Technology (DST), integrated a naturally occurring amino acid (aspartic acid) with a light-absorbing organic molecule, perylene diimide (PDI) and allowed the molecules to spontaneously organize themselves through supramolecular self-assembly.
They found that the enhanced performance arises from how the molecule organizes itself. The amino acid moiety promotes strong, extended hydrogen bonding, while the PDI chromophore drives π–π stacking and efficient light absorption.
Thus, the synergistic interplay between the two governs the molecular organization and, consequently, the functional properties of the material.
The researchers synthesised an aspartic acid-functionalized perylene diimide (PDI) molecule that spontaneously self-assembled in water into highly ordered two-dimensional nanosheets.
This subtle molecular reorganization dramatically broadened light absorption, enhanced charge separation, reduced energy losses, and increased the accessible surface area for catalytic reactions without altering the molecule's chemical composition. As a result, the self-assembled material generated nearly 18% higher photocurrent than its bulk counterpart during solar-driven water splitting.
Advanced electrochemical measurements together with density functional theory (DFT)
calculations further revealed that self-assembly promotes more efficient charge transport, while the amino acid increases the molecular dipole moment, facilitating effective separation of photo-generated charges that drive hydrogen evolution.
The study further demonstrates that naturally occurring amino acids can serve not only as molecular building blocks but also as powerful regulators of supramolecular organization and photocatalytic performance. This molecular design strategy offers a sustainable route to developing efficient, environmentally friendly, and metal-free photocatalysts for solar energy conversion.
The work led by Dr. Goutam Ghosh and Dr. Ashutosh K. Singh at the Centre for Nano and Soft Matter Sciences (CeNS), Bengaluru, together with Mr. Sourav Moyra, Mr. Kumar Shubham, and Ms. Athira Chandran M was published in the Journal of Materials Chemistry A, one of the Royal Society of Chemistry's leading journals.
Such materials could contribute to future technologies for green hydrogen production, artificial photosynthesis, solar fuel generation, and next-generation renewable energy devices, reducing dependence on costly and scarce metals.

title: TDB-DST Supports M/s Ceramat Private Limited for Commercialisation of 3D-Printed Patient-Specific Bone Grafts
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                09 SEP 2026 11:53AM by PIB Delhi
content:
Advancing India’s capabilities in high-end medical technology and strengthening indigenous alternatives to imported healthcare products, the Technology Development Board (TDB), Department of Science & Technology (DST), Government of India, has extended financial assistance to M/s Ceramat Private Limited, Palghar, Maharashtra, for the project titled “Calcium Phosphate based Standard and Customized Patient Specific Grafts by 3D Printing via Digital Light Processing Technique and Extrusion-based Equipment.” The project aims to commercialise advanced, patient-specific bone grafts using indigenously manufactured bioceramic materials and 3D printing technologies.
Ceramat Private Limited has been established with a focus on developing and commercialising indigenous technologies in bio-ceramics and advanced ceramics, with the objective of creating high-quality import substitutes for critical applications. The company’s product portfolio includes technologically intensive biomaterials such as hydroxyapatite, beta-tricalcium phosphate, biphasic calcium phosphate and bioactive glass, serving applications across orthopaedics, oral care, cosmetics and industrial sectors.
Hydroxyapatite and beta-tricalcium phosphate are calcium phosphate-based biomaterials that closely resemble the mineral composition of natural bone and are widely used in bone grafts and implant applications. A significant proportion of such advanced bone graft products available in India are currently imported. While Ceramat already manufactures bone grafts and granules through conventional processes, producing customised grafts matching the anatomy of individual patients presents a more complex manufacturing challenge.
The proposed project seeks to address this gap by integrating 3D printing with indigenously manufactured bioceramic raw materials. The company plans to develop standard as well as customised patient-specific grafts through two complementary approaches—Digital Light Processing (DLP)-based 3D printing and extrusion-based 3D printing. These technologies will enable greater flexibility in developing complex geometries and customised structures suited to specific clinical requirements.
The use of indigenous calcium phosphate-based materials in combination with advanced additive manufacturing is expected to expand Ceramet’s existing biomaterials capabilities from conventional graft products to more sophisticated, digitally designed and patient-specific solutions. The initiative will also enable the company to offer a broader range of bioceramic and orthobiological products through an integrated domestic manufacturing ecosystem.
The project is aligned with the Government of India’s emphasis on Aatmanirbhar Bharat, advanced manufacturing and indigenous medical technology development. By developing patient-specific graft manufacturing capabilities within the country, the initiative is expected to reduce dependence on imported bioceramic and orthobiological products, strengthen domestic supply chains and create a platform with potential for global markets.
Speaking on the occasion, Shri Rajesh Kumar Pathak, Secretary, TDB, said, “India’s transition from being a technology consumer to a technology developer requires indigenous capabilities in specialised and high-value areas of healthcare. The development of advanced bio-ceramics combined with 3D printing can open new possibilities for personalised medical solutions while reducing dependence on imported products. TDB is committed to supporting technologies that bring Indian innovation from development to commercial application and strengthen our capabilities in globally competitive medical manufacturing.”

content:
India is set to expand its global skills footprint with first-time participation in eleven new skill categories at the 48th WorldSkills Competition, to be held in Shanghai, China, from 22 to 27 September 2026.
Team Skill India will participate in 63 out of 64 skills, with a contingent of nearly 70 competitors, making it one of India’s largest and most diverse representations at WorldSkills to date.
The eleven new skills in which India will compete for the first time are Dental Prosthetics, Digital Interactive Media Design, Intelligent Security Technology, Landscape Gardening, Optoelectronic Technology, Retail Sales, Unmanned Aerial Systems, Industrial Mechanics, Software Testing and Heavy Vehicle Technology, Aircraft Maintenance.
India’s participation in these new categories reflects the growing depth and maturity of the country’s skilling ecosystem, which is expanding from strong foundations in traditional trades to advanced technologies, specialised services, creative industries and next-generation industrial capabilities.
The participation is being led under the aegis of the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE), with the National Skill Development Corporation (NSDC) driving India’s WorldSkills preparation through close collaboration with industry partners, training institutions and domain experts.
Speaking on India’s participation, Ms. Debashree Mukherjee, Secretary, MSDE, said,
“India’s participation in these new skills reflects the evolution of our skilling ecosystem towards future-facing and globally relevant capabilities. Through strong partnerships and rigorous preparation, we are enabling our youth to compete with confidence and benchmark themselves against global standards.”
The new categories represent emerging areas that are shaping the future of work, including healthcare technologies, digital design, intelligent systems, drone technologies, advanced manufacturing, mobility solutions and customer-centric services. Their inclusion underlines India’s focus on aligning skill development with global industry requirements and creating pathways for youth in internationally benchmarked skill domains.
Preparation for these first-time categories is being supported by a collaborative ecosystem of specialised training institutions and industry partners, including Government Tool Room and Training Centre (GTTC), Karnataka; Metrowoods Landscape; NAMTECH, Gandhinagar; Bennett University; Croma; Titan Company Ltd – Tanishq; Shoppers Stop; Reliance Trends; SANY Heavy Industry India Pvt. Ltd.; Prakhar Software Solutions Ltd.; and Denexpert Dental Lab, among others.
India’s performance in global skill competitions has shown steady progress over the years. From being ranked 29th at WorldSkills in 2015, India rose to 13th position in 2024. The country further strengthened its international performance by securing 8th rank in Asia at WorldSkills Asia 2025 and winning five medals at the Taipei Capital Cup 2026.
Under the Skill India Mission, India is building a strong preparation ecosystem anchored in industry partnerships, expert-led mentoring, structured training and global exposure. The expanded participation at WorldSkills Shanghai 2026 marks another step in India’s journey towards establishing itself as a global hub for skilled talent.

title: From Rural Aspirations to GeoAI Excellence: Dr. Panchanan Das's Journey through Higher Education
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                09 SEP 2026 6:52PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Education and innovation can open new pathways for individuals with the determination to learn and excel. Timely fellowship assistance can provide scholars with the stability and resources required to pursue advanced research and translate their knowledge into meaningful professional achievement.
Demonstrating the impact of fellowship support, Dr. Panchanan Das, a 36-year-old scholar from the Scheduled Caste community, successfully completed his Ph.D. in Remote Sensing and GIS and built a career in geospatial technology.
His journey reflects perseverance, continuous learning and the role of institutional support in enabling academic and professional advancement.
Dr. Das was raised in a rural family that valued education and hard work. His father worked as a daily wage labourer and supported the family's educational and household needs. Inspired by his family's resilience, Dr. Das remained focused on acquiring knowledge, developing specialised skills and creating better opportunities for his family.
During his academic journey, he had to manage the costs of higher education, research activities and technical resources. Delays in receiving fellowship payments during his Ph.D. added pressure and made it more difficult to maintain continuity in his studies and research work.
Growing up in a rural area also meant comparatively limited access to advanced educational facilities, professional exposure and modern technology. Opportunities for specialised training, career guidance and industry networks in emerging fields such as GIS, Remote Sensing, Artificial Intelligence and GeoAI were not readily available.
Despite these circumstances, Dr. Das remained committed to his goals. He continued to strengthen his capabilities through self-learning, research and sustained effort while balancing family responsibilities with the demands of higher education and professional development.
The scheme intervention provided financial, academic and fellowship support during his higher education and research. The assistance helped him continue his Ph.D., meet research-related requirements and enhance his technical skills in GIS, Remote Sensing, Artificial Intelligence, GeoAI and software engineering.
With the support received and his sustained dedication, Dr. Das successfully completed his Ph.D. in Remote Sensing and GIS. He is currently working with Uncharted AI as a Software Engineer and GeoAI Expert in Mapping and GIS, contributing to projects involving geospatial technologies, LiDAR and route optimisation.
His professional employment has enabled him to attain financial stability and support his family while continuing to grow in a specialised technology field. The transition from a rural academic environment to a career in GeoAI demonstrates how education and appropriate institutional assistance can expand professional opportunities.
Looking ahead, Dr. Das aspires to further develop his expertise in GeoAI and software engineering. He also aims to contribute to research and innovation through people-centric technological solutions in remote sensing, drone technology and geospatial analytics for wider public benefit.
Dr. Panchanan Das's journey highlights the transformative role of education, fellowship support and continuous skill development. His achievement stands as an inspiring example of ambition and perseverance strengthened by institutional support and professional opportunity.

title: From Sanitation Professional to Self-Reliant Entrepreneur: Shri Dharmendra Kumar Ray's Journey under NAMASTE-SUY
date:

content:
Skill, experience and determination can create meaningful pathways to entrepreneurship. With timely access to financial assistance and mechanised equipment, sanitation professionals can translate their expertise into sustainable livelihoods while securing a better future for their families.
Shri Dharmendra Kumar Ray, a 39-year-old sanitation professional from Bihar, has built his journey through practical learning, sustained effort and a clear aspiration to become self-employed.
Having studied up to the sixth standard, he developed specialised experience in sewer and septic tank cleaning operations and used the support available under the NAMASTE Scheme to establish his own mechanised sanitation service.
To strengthen his technical capabilities, Shri Ray worked for nearly four years as a Helper and Graver Machine Operator with Shiva and Shiva Company in Noida. During this period, he acquired practical knowledge of operating and maintaining sewer-cleaning machinery and gained valuable experience in sanitation services.
His experience encouraged him to pursue self-employment and create a more secure livelihood for his family. However, the cost of procuring specialised machinery and a suitable vehicle remained a major constraint in turning this aspiration into an enterprise.
Under the Swachhta Udyami Yojana component of the NAMASTE Scheme, Shri Ray received financial assistance in the form of an upfront capital subsidy for purchasing a Jetting Cum Graver Machine along with a Mahindra Maxx City CBC 1.3 LX vehicle. The total project cost was Rs. 14,77,500, comprising a loan of Rs. 7,38,750 and a capital subsidy of Rs. 7,38,750.
With this assistance, he established his own mechanised sanitation service. The machine has been deployed under the Greater Noida Authority for sewer and septic tank cleaning operations, enabling him to use his technical skills as a self-reliant entrepreneur and secure sustainable livelihood opportunities.
Following the scheme intervention, Shri Ray's monthly income increased by approximately Rs. 25,000 to Rs. 30,000 through independent sanitation work. The improvement in his financial position enabled him to bring his wife and two children from Bihar to Noida so that the family could live together.
He has also enrolled his children in a good school in Noida, ensuring access to better education and opportunities for a brighter future. The support has strengthened the family's economic security and contributed to a more stable and dignified quality of life.
From an experienced sanitation professional to a self-reliant entrepreneur, Shri Dharmendra Kumar Ray's journey reflects the transformative impact of the NAMASTE-SUY initiative. His success demonstrates how practical skills, determination and institutional support can combine to create sustainable livelihoods, strengthen families and advance mechanised sanitation services.

, the scheme strengthens infrastructure, pedagogy, inclusion, and sustainability, while equipping students with 21st-century skills. As of July 2026,
13,092 schools
- around 90% of the target- have been selected across 36 States/UTs including schools under KVS, NVS, and NCERT. The schools are selected through a three-stage Challenge Mode based on defined quality benchmarks. Envisioned as mentor institutions for neighbouring schools, PM SHRI schools mark a shift from infrastructure-centric development towards holistic, equitable, and future-ready education.
PM SHRI: Building Schools That Lead by Example
India is witnessing a significant transformation in its school education system, marked by a growing emphasis on quality, equity, inclusion, and future-ready learning. With
14.71 lakh
schools serving more than
24.69 crore
students, the education system is increasingly focused on enhancing learning outcomes and creating enabling environments that support the holistic development of every learner. The
National Education Policy (NEP) 2020
furnishes the overarching framework for this transformation, while the PM SHRI initiative operationalizes its vision at the school level, translating policy intent into institutional practice.
Launched on
7 September 2022
, the Pradhan Mantri Schools for Rising India (PM SHRI) Scheme
is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme implemented by the Department of School Education and Literacy, Ministry of Education
.
The scheme seeks to qualitatively strengthen existing schools and develop them as exemplar institutions demonstrating the effective implementation of the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020
.
With a total project cost of
₹
27,360 crore
, the scheme focuses on strengthening
more than 14,500 existing schools
as exemplar institutions. These schools are envisioned to provide
safe, stimulating, and welcoming learning environments
, supported by quality infrastructure, appropriate learning resources, and diverse learning experiences.
As of July 2026,
13,092 schools have been selected
as PM SHRI Schools across States and Union Territories, including schools under the
Kendriya Vidyalaya Sangathan (KVS), Navodaya Vidyalaya Samiti (NVS) and National Council of Educational Research and Training (NCERT)
. This represents around
90% of the envisaged target
. The scheme is expected to benefit more than 20 lakh students directly.
Strategic Focus of PM SHRI
The scheme extends support beyond strengthening individual schools. PM SHRI schools are envisioned as
models for their regions
, sharing their practices and supporting neighbouring schools through
mentoring, handholding, collaboration and clustering
. This is intended to create a ripple effect, enabling more schools to develop towards exemplar standards over time.
At the core of the scheme is a vision of education that fosters
lifelong learning
and equips students with the capacity and disposition to learn, unlearn and relearn. The broader objective is to develop engaged, productive and responsible citizens capable of contributing to the creation of an
equitable, inclusive and plural society.
Strengthening School Education Through PM SHRI
The
Pradhan Mantri Schools for Rising India (PM SHRI)
scheme is being implemented over
five years, from 2022–23 to 2026–27
. The scheme has a total project cost of
₹
27,360 crore
, including a
Central share of
₹
18,128 crore
. The central share of approved
Project Approval Board (PAB) outlay
rose from
₹
2,520 crore in 2023–24 to
₹
5,224 crore in 2026–27
. This marks an increase of around
107%
, reflecting the growing scale of investment in strengthening PM SHRI schools.
PM SHRI Schools: Advancing the Vision of NEP 2020
PM SHRI Scheme aims to showcase all the components of the National Education Policy 2020 and focuses not only on cognitive development but also on creating holistic and well-rounded individuals equipped with key 21st century skills. The scheme focuses on creating an equitable, inclusive, and joyful learning environment that caters to diverse backgrounds and varied academic abilities. These schools are designed to engage students actively in their learning process, ensuring that every child feels welcomed, cared for, and supported in a safe and stimulating environment.
Key Dimensions of Quality and Excellence under PM SHRI
PM SHRI Schools are designed as exemplar schools that demonstrate the key principles of NEP 2020 through quality education, modern infrastructure, inclusive practices and sustainable development.
Inclusive Learning:
Provides high-quality, equitable, and joyful education while addressing diverse backgrounds, multilingual needs, and different learning abilities.
Mentorship:
PM SHRI Schools will serve as exemplar schools and provide leadership and mentorship to other schools in their regions.
Green Schools:
Promote sustainable and environment-friendly practices as an important school quality benchmark.
Experiential Learning:
Emphasizes experiential, holistic, integrated, inquiry-based, and learner-centered approaches, including play and toy-based learning in the foundational years.
Learning Outcomes:
Focuses on curriculum, pedagogy and assessment to strengthen learning outcomes and the application of knowledge.
Quality Infrastructure:
Involves assessing school infrastructure on parameters including
adequacy, functionality, aesthetics and safety
.
Future Ready Skills:
Promotes exposure to
21st century skills
and links schools with the local entrepreneurial ecosystem.
Quality Assessment:
The
School Quality Assessment Framework (SQAF)
provides a structured mechanism to assess and monitor the quality of PM SHRI Schools.

How PM SHRI Schools Transform School Education
Learning Designed Around the Child
PM SHRI schools follow either the CBSE or the relevant State or Union Territory syllabus according to their affiliation. Their curriculum follows the National Curriculum Framework or State Curriculum Framework developed in accordance with the 5+3+3+4 curricular and pedagogical structure under NEP 2020. States and Union Territories have flexibility to contextualise the curriculum according to local needs while adhering to core principles and constitutional values.
PM SHRI Schools also promote experiential learning through bagless days,
internships with local artisans, study of local arts, crafts and traditions, celebration of important cultural events, and preservation of indigenous knowledge and practices.
Equity, Inclusion and Multilingual Learning
PMSHRI schools have played a pivotal role in providing inclusive and equitable education, ensuring that students from diverse backgrounds, including rural and underserved communities, have access to high-quality education. By focusing on bridging educational disparities, these schools have helped create a more equitable learning environment across India.
The scheme also promotes the use of the
mother tongue, local or regional language as the medium of teaching and learning, particularly in the early grades
. The latest UDISE+ 2025–26 data records 6,102 Sanskrit teachers, 1,994 Urdu teachers, and 9,152 regional language teachers in PM SHRI schools.
It also encourages community participation in supporting learning through local languages. This approach is crucial for ensuring that every child develops strong
foundational literacy and numeracy skills
.
Technology Enabled Learning
A significant achievement of PM SHRI Schools lies in the systematic integration of technology into the teaching–learning environment. The provision of Information and Communication Technology (ICT) facilities, smart classrooms, internet connectivity, digital learning platforms, and STEM-based programmes is contributing to the creation of more interactive, experiential, and learner-centred educational environments. These interventions not only enhance access to diverse learning resources but also support the development of digital literacy, technological competencies, critical thinking, and problem-solving skills. Platforms such as DIKSHA serve as repositories of high-quality digital educational resources and facilitate the sharing and dissemination of learning materials among teachers and students, thereby strengthening technology-enabled pedagogical practices.
Holistic Student Development
PM SHRI Schools adopt a holistic approach to student development by integrating academic learning with extracurricular activities, sports, arts, and life-skills education. This multidimensional approach extends beyond conventional academic achievement to foster the development of leadership capabilities, creativity, socio-emotional competencies, and interpersonal skills. By providing opportunities for diverse forms of learning and participation, the schools seek to equip students with the competencies, resilience, and adaptability required to navigate future educational, professional, and social challenges.
Empowering Teachers and School Leaders
PM SHRI Schools seek to strengthen teacher capacity and institutional leadership through structured professional development initiatives supported by District Institutes of Education and Training (DIETs). Under the initiative, financial assistance of up to ₹3 lakh per DIET is provided for capacity-building programmes, while support of up to ₹2,500 per teacher is extended for the training of subject teachers, principals, special educators, ICT teachers, and master trainers.
Principals are provided training in educational leadership, school management, and competency-based pedagogical planning, enabling them to strengthen institutional planning and academic governance. Teachers receive professional development in areas including the Holistic Progress Card, school safety, mental health and well-being, first-level counselling, and ICT integration. These interventions seek to enhance pedagogical competencies, strengthen school leadership, and promote continuous professional development among educational personnel.
A Growing National Network
The PM SHRI initiative has established a substantial national network comprising
13,092 selected schools
across States and Union Territories, including institutions under the
Kendriya Vidyalaya Sangathan (KVS), Navodaya Vidyalaya Samiti (NVS), and National Council of Educational Research and Training (NCERT).
The initiative has achieved extensive geographical coverage, encompassing
725 districts and 8,340 blocks/ULBs
, thereby establishing a broad institutional and spatial footprint across the country.
Among the
13,092 selected schools, 1,305 are primary schools, 3,102 upper primary schools, 3,141 secondary schools, and 5,544 higher secondary schools
. The network further includes 80 Kasturba Gandhi Balika Vidyalayas (KGBVs), 913 KVS schools, 620 NVS schools, and 4 NCERT schools. The scale and diversity of this network demonstrate the expanding reach of PM SHRI Schools.
Selection Built on Quality Benchmarks
Selection of PM SHRI schools is done through Challenge Mode, wherein Schools compete for support to become exemplar schools. Selection is done through a three-stage process with definite timelines, which is as follows:
Stage 1: Signing of Memorandum of Understanding (MoU)
States and Union Territories (UTs) enter into a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the Centre, outlining their commitments towards providing the requisite support and enabling the selected schools to achieve the prescribed quality standards for PM SHRI Schools.
Stage 2: Identification of Eligible Schools
A pool of schools eligible for selection as PM SHRI Schools is identified on the basis of prescribed minimum benchmarks and relevant indicators available through the UDISE+ data.
Stage 3: Selection through the Challenge Method
Eligible schools identified in Stage 2 participate in a challenge-based selection process to demonstrate compliance with specified criteria. Schools compete against the prescribed challenge conditions, with fulfilment of the stipulated requirements.
Fulfillment of conditions is verified and certified through physical inspection by the respective States/UTs, KVS, or NVS authorities, and recommend the list of schools to the Ministry.
An Expert Committee headed by the Secretary (SE&L), at the Ministry of Education, is constituted for final selection of schools. Schools must meet minimum standards such as a
pucca building, barrier-free access, safety measures, separate toilets, drinking water, hand-washing facilities, electricity, ID cards for teachers, enrolment at Elementary and Senior Secondary levels must be more than the State average enrolment and library or sports facilities
. For the Challenge Method, schools in urban areas are required to secure a minimum score of 70 percent, while schools in rural areas require a minimum of 60 percent. The assessment covers
infrastructure, learning outcomes, pedagogy, PM POSHAN, vocational education, green initiatives, and stakeholder commitment
.
Schools as Models for Wider Change
PM SHRI represents a paradigm shift from an
infrastructure-centric approach to school development
towards the establishment of holistic, inclusive, equitable, and future-ready learning institutions. The initiative operationalises the vision and priorities of the
National Education Policy (NEP) 2020
by emphasising quality and competency-based learning, continuous teacher professional development, technology-enabled education, and the creation of a safe, inclusive, and enabling school environment.
As exemplar institutions, PM SHRI Schools are envisaged to
demonstrate and disseminate innovative educational practices
that can be adapted and replicated by neighbouring schools, thereby contributing to broader systemic improvements in school education. The overarching objective is to foster capable, confident, creative, and responsible learners, equipped with the knowledge, skills, and values required to participate meaningfully in a
more equitable, inclusive, and future-ready India
.

title: NHRC, India takes suo motu cognizance of the reported perils of school children forced to cross a river through an unfinished bridge in the Mainpur Block area of Gariyaband district in Chhattisgarh
subtitle:
Issues a notice to the Chhattisgarh Chief Secretary, calling for a detailed report on the matter within two weeks

The bridge remains incomplete despite being under construction for nearly six years
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                09 SEP 2026 4:43PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC), India has taken
suo motu
cognizance of a media report that dozens of children from Khambhatha and nearby settlements in the Mainpur Block area of Gariyaband district in Chhattisgarh, are compelled to climb a narrow and slippery iron ladder, attached to an unfinished bridge, to cross the Paiririver to reach their schools. Reportedly, the monsoon turns the shallow river into a torrent.
The Commission has observed that the contents of the media report, if true, raise serious issues of violation of human rights. Therefore, it has issued a notice to the Chief Secretary, Government of Chhattisgarh, calling for a detailed report on the matter within two weeks.
According to the media report, carried on 3rd September 2026, a roughly 300-metre-long bridge between Deharguda and Khambhatha in Mainpur Block has been under construction for nearly six years despite the villagers having been assured of its completion in six months by the concerned authorities about a year ago.
